questions.question: Q1. What does State of Health (SoH) represent in a lithium-ion battery pack?

answers.a: The instantaneous electrical charge currently remaining in the cells.
answers.b: The performance capability of the battery relative to its brand-new specifications.
answers.c: The rate of volumetric cooling fluid flowing across the bottom plate loop.
answers.d: The structural mechanical force holding the modules inside the chassis.

explanations.a: Instantaneous charge is represented by State of Charge (SoC).
explanations.b: Correct. State of Health (SoH) compares maximum deliverable capacity to baseline new capacity.
explanations.c: Cooling fluid flow is a thermal management metric.
explanations.d: Mechanical clamping force is a structural packaging property.

questions.question: Q2. Which boundary threshold typically defines the End-of-Life (EOL) condition for electric vehicle battery packs?

explanations.b: 85% SoH represents active degradation but not automotive retirement.
explanations.c: Correct. 70% to 80% SoH is widely established as automotive End-of-Life (EOL) threshold.
explanations.d: 50% SoH is well beyond EV retirement standards into second-life applications.

questions.question: Q3. Continuous growth of the Solid Electrolyte Interphase (SEI) layer directly impacts the battery pack by doing which of the following?

answers.a: Increasing total cyclable lithium ions and reducing core heat flux.
answers.b: Consuming active lithium ions and driving capacity fade.
answers.c: Lowering internal resistance and improving thermal safety margins.
answers.d: Accelerating coolant velocity within the liquid cooling plates.

explanations.a: SEI growth consumes active lithium, reducing cyclable ions.
explanations.b: Correct. SEI layer growth consumes mobile lithium ions and increases internal impedance, causing capacity fade.
explanations.c: SEI thickening increases internal resistance, not lowering it.
explanations.d: Coolant velocity is controlled by external cooling pumps.

questions.question: Q4. What is Joule heating (thermal flux) inside a battery pack directly caused by?

answers.a: Passage of electrical current through the internal cell resistance.
answers.b: External ambient temperature matching standard laboratory baseline conditions.
answers.c: The mechanical expansion of mounting flanges on the chassis frame.
answers.d: The conversion of cyclable lithium back into gaseous electrolytes.

explanations.a: Correct. Joule heating is calculated as P_loss = I^2 * R_int.
explanations.b: Ambient temperature is an external boundary condition.
explanations.c: Mechanical expansion does not generate electrical resistive heat.
explanations.d: Electrolyte gassing is a degradation symptom, not the source of resistive heating.

questions.question: Q5. How is a C-rate of 3C contextually defined regarding a battery pack's operation?

answers.a: It takes 3 hours to discharge or charge the battery fully.
answers.b: The battery pack operates at exactly 3 times the baseline resistance.
answers.c: A fast charging rate that fully charges the battery in 20 minutes under maximum current.
answers.d: The thermal dissipation scaling index reaches a value of 3.0x.

explanations.a: A 3-hour charge corresponds to C/3 rate.
explanations.b: C-rate defines current scale relative to nominal capacity, not internal resistance.
explanations.c: Correct. 3C rate discharges/charges full capacity in 1/3 of an hour (20 minutes).
explanations.d: Thermal scaling is an operational byproduct, not the definition of C-rate.
